title: Power
blurb: Watts are amperes times volts: P = I × E.

lines.caption: Power is the rate at which electrical energy is used.
Power equals current times voltage: P = I × E.
Say a radio draws 10 amperes from a 13.8 volt power supply.
10 times 13.8 is 138. The radio is using 138 watts.
You can turn the formula around. To find current, divide power by voltage.
So 120 watts at 12 volts takes 10 amperes.
